title: AsRef Interface
concept: AsRef converts a reference to your type into a reference to another type — enabling flexible APIs that accept multiple input types.
why: Without AsRef, functions that need a &Str can only accept &Str. With AsRef, they accept &Str, &String, &Path, and any type convertible to &Str.
tips: Implement AsRef when you need multiple reference conversions — Deref only gives one
Use AsRef bounds on generic function parameters to accept many input types
AsRef is cheap — it just returns a reference, no allocation
Prefer AsRef over requiring callers to manually convert types
common_mistakes: Confusing AsRef with From — AsRef borrows, From owns (allocates)
Implementing AsRef for expensive conversions — AsRef should be O(1), just a pointer cast
Not implementing AsRef when your type clearly 'is' another type — limits API usability
